content.user_title: Configure PixiJS for Workers, SSR, and Strict CSP
content.value_statement: PixiJS applications can fail when browser APIs are unavailable or security policies block dynamic compilation. This skill guides adapter selection, worker setup, and CSP-compatible initialization.
actual_capabilities: Explain OffscreenCanvas transfer and PixiJS initialization inside a module worker.
Guide DOMAdapter selection and configuration before renderer initialization.
Outline custom Adapter methods for Node.js, headless testing, and SSR environments.
Explain the pixi.js/unsafe-eval compatibility import for strict CSP without enabling unsafe evaluation.
Compare browser and worker subpath imports with loadEnvironmentExtensions configuration.
Identify browser-global usage and obsolete settings.ADAPTER configuration that break environment portability.
limitations: Provides documentation and examples, not an executable renderer or automated compatibility tests.
Requires suitable canvas and graphics implementations for headless rendering; the adapter example does not supply every runtime dependency.
Worker rendering depends on OffscreenCanvas support and cannot provide DOM overlays or DOM-based accessibility.
Focuses on PixiJS v8; examples require checking against the installed package version and bundler configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Understand environment adapters
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain when PixiJS v8 needs BrowserAdapter, WebWorkerAdapter, or a custom Adapter. Describe when to call DOMAdapter.set.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: choose an adapter before changing application code.

prompt_templates.title: Set up worker rendering
prompt_templates.prompt: Help move my PixiJS v8 renderer into a module worker using OffscreenCanvas. Cover canvas transfer, adapter setup, imports, and unsupported DOM features.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: move browser rendering away from the main thread.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a strict CSP failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my PixiJS v8 imports and CSP initialization error. Explain the pixi.js/unsafe-eval module and recommend changes without relaxing the security policy.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: troubleshoot renderer initialization under strict CSP.

prompt_templates.title: Review a custom headless adapter
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my PixiJS v8 custom Adapter for Node.js tests. Check required methods, unavailable globals, graphics dependencies, extension loading, and initialization order.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: evaluate a custom runtime integration before implementation.

output_examples.input: My PixiJS worker fails because document is unavailable. What should I review?
output: Transfer an OffscreenCanvas from the main thread to the worker.
Replace direct browser-global access with adapter methods.
Keep DOM overlays and DOM-based accessibility outside the worker.

output_examples.input: PixiJS reports that my environment does not allow unsafe-eval. Must I weaken CSP?
output: Import the PixiJS unsafe-eval compatibility module before renderer initialization.
The module provides static polyfills rather than enabling unsafe evaluation.
Verify the import remains in the production bundle and retest initialization.

output_examples.input: Can I use the custom adapter example directly for Node.js rendering?
output: Treat the example as an integration outline, not a complete runtime.
Supply compatible canvas, image, XML parsing, and graphics implementations.
Verify that referenced rendering context constructors exist in your runtime.
Test renderer initialization and asset loading before adding application features.

best_practices: Set the environment adapter before creating and initializing the PixiJS application.
Use adapter methods instead of browser globals in code shared across environments.
Load CSP compatibility imports before renderer initialization and verify behavior under the deployed security policy.
anti_patterns: Changing DOMAdapter only after the renderer has initialized.
Assuming worker or SSR environments provide document, Image, or DOM accessibility features.
Enabling unsafe evaluation in CSP instead of checking the documented compatibility import.

faq.question: Which PixiJS version does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It targets PixiJS v8 and explains adapter configuration changes from older settings-based patterns.

faq.question: Does pixi.js/unsafe-eval enable unsafe evaluation?
faq.answer: No. The documented module replaces dynamic code generation with static polyfills for environments that block unsafe evaluation.

faq.question: When should I configure DOMAdapter?
faq.answer: Configure it before renderer initialization. Setting it before creating the application also keeps startup order clear.

faq.question: Can all PixiJS features run in a worker?
faq.answer: No. DOM overlays and DOM-based accessibility require browser DOM access. Worker rendering also requires suitable OffscreenCanvas support.

faq.question: Does the skill provide a complete Node.js renderer?
faq.answer: No. It outlines a custom Adapter, but you must supply compatible canvas, graphics, image, and XML implementations.

faq.question: How should I choose environment-specific imports?
faq.answer: Use browser or worker subpaths for static module registration. Review loadEnvironmentExtensions when controlling automatic environment extension loading.
